docs.text: Admin ¶ OpenImport lives under System › Data Transfer : OpenImport Profiles and OpenImport Runs . Settings are under Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport . Profiles ¶ The profile list shows each profile's direction, what it imports or exports, its source, schedule and last run. Row actions: Edit , Dry run , Run now , Duplicate (the copy starts with its schedule off) and Delete (runs and error reports are kept). The profile form has six steps: What : name, import or export, and what (Products, Stock & prices, Customers …). Where : the source. For Upload a file , choose the file; it is read on the server, never in the browser. File : format and its options (delimiter, encoding, sheet, record path). The first 20 rows of the file are shown and read again when an option changes. Map : one row per Magento field: the column of the file (or a fixed value), the store view, transforms (add, move up and down, remove), required , and a value map. Auto-match proposes a mapping from the column names (and adds Decimal comma → dot where the file writes numbers with commas), Add required fields adds what Magento needs for new records with proposed fixed values, Preview the first rows shows what Magento will receive, row by row, with any problems. Rules : behaviour, rows with errors, allowed errors, skip unchanged rows (delta), safety limit, row filters. When : manual or a schedule (presets or a cron expression), schedule on/off, e-mails, what happens to the source file after a successful run. Save and dry run saves and starts a dry run straight away. New profiles have their schedule off; switch it on after a dry run you are happy with. Runs ¶ Runs are queued and run by OpenImport's cron within a minute (or by bin/magento openimport:run ). The run page shows the status, the numbers (rows read, new, changed, unchanged, skipped, errors), and refreshes itself while the run is queued or running. Dry runs list what would change: for each record the field, the value now and the value after the run. Run for real imports the very file the dry run checked. Runs with Delete or Replace above the safety limit need the word DELETE or REPLACE typed in, by a role allowed to confirm them ( Confirm runs above the safety limit ). Download error report gives a CSV with the row number, record, field and error, followed by the original row, so you can fix the rows and import them again. Cells that a spreadsheet would run as formulas are protected. Download the file gives the file the run read. A queued run can be cancelled. Permissions ¶ Resource Allows View profiles the profile list and form (read only) Create and edit profiles saving, duplicating and deleting profiles, uploading files Run profiles dry runs, live runs, cancelling queued runs Confirm runs above the safety limit the typed confirmation for Delete and Replace View runs and error reports the run list, run pages and downloads

docs.text: REST API and triggers ¶ Since 1.1. Start a profile from another system ¶ POST /rest/V1/openimport/profiles/{profileId}/runs Authorization: Bearer <integration access token> Content-Type: application/json {"mode": "live"} mode is dry_run (default) or live . The run is queued with the trigger API and OpenImport's cron runs it within a minute, exactly like a scheduled run: same source, mapping, delta, safety threshold (a live run above it waits for a confirmation in the admin) and e-mails. Import profiles need a source other than Upload (folder, URL, SFTP or FTP); exports work with every destination. Answer: {"run_id": 42, "status": "queued", "mode": "live", "message": "", "rows_read": 0, "errors": 0} Ask how it went: GET /rest/V1/openimport/runs/{runId} Access: create an integration (System › Extensions › Integrations) with the resources OpenImport › Run profiles (start) and View runs and error reports (status). Typical use: a PIM or ERP drops a file on the SFTP server and then calls the endpoint, so the import starts at once instead of at the next schedule. Export right after an order is placed ¶ Order export profiles have the setting Also run after every order . When an order is placed (storefront, admin or API), the profile is queued; cron runs it within a minute. Ten orders in that minute make one run, not ten. Combine it with Which orders: Only orders not exported before by this profile so every file holds just the new orders.

docs.text: Product attributes and attribute sets ¶ Since 1.1. Entity Product attributes and attribute sets ( openimport_attribute ), identifier attribute_code . Import ¶ Add/Update creates attributes that do not exist and updates the given columns of existing ones; it also assigns the attribute to attribute sets. Delete takes the attribute out of the listed attribute sets only: OpenImport never deletes an attribute (its values on every product would go with it). Replace is refused. Column Meaning attribute_code identifier; lower-case letters, digits, underscores label default label; required for a new attribute frontend_input text , textarea , texteditor , select , multiselect , boolean , date , datetime , price , weight ; required for a new attribute, cannot change later options Cotton|Wool|Silk for select and multiselect; options the attribute lacks are added, existing ones keep their ids and order scope global , website or store is_required , is_unique , is_searchable , is_filterable_in_search , is_comparable , is_visible_on_front , used_in_product_listing , is_html_allowed_on_front , is_used_for_promo_rules , used_for_sort_by 1 / 0 (also yes / no , true / false , ja / nein ) is_filterable 0 , 1 (filterable with results) or 2 (filterable, no results) default_value text attribute_set Default, Bags : the sets to assign the attribute to (they must exist) attribute_group the group inside those sets; created when missing; default General Store-view labels work like everywhere in OpenImport: map a file column to store:<store view code>:label for the attribute's label and to store:<store view code>:options for the option labels, in the order of the default options ( Baumwolle|Wolle|Seide ; leave an entry empty to keep the default). The dry run shows the attributes that would be created and every column that would change. Writes go through Magento's attribute repository and attribute management, so the same validation as the admin applies. Export ¶ One row per attribute of the shop's own (user-defined) attributes with options, flags and the sets it belongs to, plus one row per store view with its own label or option labels. Export option attributes = all adds Magento's system attributes. The file imports back as it is.

docs.text: Baseline: core import speed and the core bridge's overhead ¶ Measured in M0 so every later speed claim compares against Magento's own importer, never against another vendor. Method. openimport-dev-env/ci/benchmark.php in the dev-env's Benchmark workflow: Magento Open Source 2.4.9, PHP 8.3, MariaDB 10.6, OpenSearch 2.12, Redis, no sample data, all indexers on "Update by Schedule" , a GitHub Actions runner (4 vCPU, 16 GB). Datasets are generated deterministically by ci/generate-datasets.php : products-10k : 10,000 simple products, 3 categories each (created on the fly), stock, price, a special price on every 7th, an HTML description, plus a German store-view row on every 10th product (11,000 rows); customers-20k : 20,000 customers with one default address ( customer_composite ). Each dataset is imported twice through core's CSV source (create, then the same file again = every entity updated, no value changes) and twice through OpenImport's MappedSource (same rows, other SKUs / e-mails / names). All passes run in one PHP process, so peak memory grows from pass to pass and is shown for orientation only. Results (run 38403542694 , 2026-10-13) ¶ Dataset Path Pass Rows Created Updated Seconds Rows / min products-10k core CSV create 11,000 10,000 10 87.0 7,584 products-10k core CSV update 11,000 0 11,000 89.6 7,363 products-10k OpenImport create 11,000 10,000 10 86.1 7,670 products-10k OpenImport update 11,000 0 11,000 91.8 7,191 customers-20k core CSV create 20,000 20,000 0 24.5 49,077 customers-20k core CSV update 20,000 0 20,000 25.2 47,623 customers-20k OpenImport create 20,000 20,000 0 26.5 45,299 customers-20k OpenImport update 20,000 0 20,000 27.0 44,447 What it says ¶ The core bridge costs almost nothing: products −1 % / +2.5 %, customers +8 % / +7 % (reading the CSV in PHP and building associative rows). The budget in 02 · Architecture is 15 % for the whole pipeline. Re-importing an unchanged catalog costs as much as creating it (90 s for 10k products). A nightly supplier file usually changes a few percent of the rows: delta mode (M1) skips unchanged rows before core sees them. Target: a run with 1 % changed rows takes at most 10 % of a full run. Rate: about 7,500 product rows or 48,000 customer rows per minute on a CI runner with indexers on schedule. Shops with "Update on Save" indexers will be slower; openimport:doctor warns about it. 50,000 products: see below. Configurable products and the full pipeline (readers, mapping, delta) are measured at the end of M1 (memory flat from 10k to 50k is an M1 done-when). 50,000 products (run 38403706606 , 2026-10-13) ¶ Same method, products-50k (50,000 simple products plus 5,000 German store-view rows = 55,000 rows). Path Pass Rows Created Updated Seconds Rows / min core CSV create 55,000 50,000 50 438.6 7,523 core CSV update 55,000 0 55,000 471.6 6,997 OpenImport create 55,000 50,000 50 453.8 7,272 OpenImport update 55,000 0 55,000 497.1 6,639 Core's rate stays flat from 10k to 50k (about 7,500 rows per minute): no slowdown with catalog size at this scale. Bridge overhead +3.5 % (create) and +5.4 % (update), inside the 15 % budget. Peak memory is not comparable between passes here (one process, four passes). The M1 memory check runs each pass in its own process. The whole pipeline (M1, run 38518924669 and 38422135458 , 2026-10-14) ¶ openimport-dev-env/ci/pipeline-benchmark.php : a profile that maps every column 1:1 with transforms on sku, url_key and name, delta on; every pass in its own PHP process ( bin/magento openimport:run ), so peak memory is comparable. Core's own CSV import of the same file runs the same way as the reference. Dataset Pass Read Created Updated Unchanged Seconds Peak MB products-10k core CSV create (reference) 11,000 10,000 10 – 127.0 123 products-10k core CSV update (reference) 11,000 0 11,000 – 138.8 171 products-10k dry run 11,000 11,000 would be new 10.0 119 products-10k import (create) 11,000 10,000 10 0 126.7 183 products-10k same file again (delta) 11,000 0 0 11,000 1.4 87 products-10k same file, --full 11,000 0 11,000 0 144.1 231 products-10k 1 % changed (100 rows, delta) 11,000 0 100 10,900 3.1 121 products-50k core CSV create (reference) 55,000 50,000 50 – 560.8 344 products-50k core CSV update (reference) 55,000 0 55,000 – 643.2 553 products-50k dry run 55,000 55,000 would be new 38.2 180 products-50k import (create) 55,000 50,000 50 0 586.9 425 products-50k same file again (delta) 55,000 0 0 55,000 4.8 89 products-50k same file, --full 55,000 0 55,000 0 679.8 625 products-50k 1 % changed (500 rows, delta) 55,000 0 500 54,500 12.6 140 Overhead of the whole pipeline (read CSV, map, transform, spool, delta hashes, error mapping) against core's own CSV import: create −0.2 % (10k) / +4.7 % (50k), update +3.8 % / +5.7 %. Budget: 15 %. Delta: a nightly file with 1 % changed rows takes 2.1 % (10k) / 1.9 % (50k) of a full re-import. Target: 10 %. An unchanged file costs 1–5 seconds instead of 2–11 minutes. (A first run found that store-view lines were always resent: each line now has its own hash.) Memory: OpenImport's own part is flat: the delta pass needs 87 MB at 10k and 89 MB at 50k, the dry run 119 and 180 MB. The live import's peak follows core's import model (123 → 344 MB for core's own CSV import, 183 → 425 MB through OpenImport, a steady 60–80 MB on top); that growth is core's catalog cache, not the pipeline's. docs.text: Categories ¶ Since 1.1. Import and export categories by path : the names from the root category down, joined with / ( Default Category/Men/Shoes ). A slash inside a name is written \/ . Paths are matched ignoring case; the first segment must be a root category of the shop. Import ¶ Entity Categories ( openimport_category ), behaviours Add/Update and Delete (Replace is refused: Magento would delete and recreate the categories with new ids). Column Meaning path identifier; parents that do not exist yet are created on the way (active, in the menu, named after the segment) name a new category is named after the last segment of its path (a different name is refused, it would make the next import create a duplicate); for an existing category the name column renames it, and its path changes with it url_key , description , meta_title , meta_keywords , meta_description , custom_design , page_layout texts is_active , include_in_menu , is_anchor 1 / 0 , also yes / no , true / false , ja / nein position whole number display_mode PRODUCTS , PAGE or PRODUCTS_AND_PAGE Only the columns a row has are changed, and an empty cell leaves the value as it is ( __EMPTY__VALUE__ clears a default value, as in Magento's import; a name or URL key cannot be cleared). Store-view values are saved one attribute at a time, so a German name does not regenerate the category's URL rewrites (change url_key for that). Store-view values work like everywhere in OpenImport: map a file column to store:<store view code>:<field> ( name_de → Store view de , field name ) and the row sets that store view's value. A shop with only one store view keeps every value in the default scope (that is how Magento saves), so there store-view rows are reported as errors: map the column to the default field instead. The dry run shows the categories that would be created and every field that would change; delete runs count the children too and wait for the typed confirmation above the safety threshold. Writes go through Magento's category model and repository (URL rewrites, indexers and events happen as in the admin), never through raw SQL. Products are assigned to categories through the product import ( categories column), not here. Export ¶ Entity Categories , one row per category with its default values, plus one row per store view that overrides any text ( store_view_code set, only the overridden columns filled). Export option category_rows = default writes default rows only. The file imports back as it is.

docs.text: Entity Categories ( openimport_category ), behaviours Add/Update and Delete (Replace is refused: Magento would delete and recreate the categories with new ids). Column Meaning path identifier; parents that do not exist yet are created on the way (active, in the menu, named after the segment) name a new category is named after the last segment of its path (a different name is refused, it would make the next import create a duplicate); for an existing category the name column renames it, and its path changes with it url_key , description , meta_title , meta_keywords , meta_description , custom_design , page_layout texts is_active , include_in_menu , is_anchor 1 / 0 , also yes / no , true / false , ja / nein position whole number display_mode PRODUCTS , PAGE or PRODUCTS_AND_PAGE Only the columns a row has are changed, and an empty cell leaves the value as it is ( __EMPTY__VALUE__ clears a default value, as in Magento's import; a name or URL key cannot be cleared). Store-view values are saved one attribute at a time, so a German name does not regenerate the category's URL rewrites (change url_key for that). Store-view values work like everywhere in OpenImport: map a file column to store:<store view code>:<field> ( name_de → Store view de , field name ) and the row sets that store view's value. A shop with only one store view keeps every value in the default scope (that is how Magento saves), so there store-view rows are reported as errors: map the column to the default field instead. The dry run shows the categories that would be created and every field that would change; delete runs count the children too and wait for the typed confirmation above the safety threshold. Writes go through Magento's category model and repository (URL rewrites, indexers and events happen as in the admin), never through raw SQL. Products are assigned to categories through the product import ( categories column), not here.

Option Effect --dry-run Check and preview only; nothing changes in the shop. --file=path Read this file instead of the profile's source. --full Ignore the delta state: send every row. --confirm Confirm a Delete or Replace run above the safety threshold. --queue Only add the run to the queue; OpenImport's cron runs it. The exit code is 0 for Success and Partial , 1 otherwise, so the command can be used in scripts and deployment pipelines. openimport:run:status ¶ Shows any run (also runs started in the admin or by a schedule) with its counts, changes and errors. openimport:profile:list ¶ Lists all profiles with direction, entity, source, schedule, whether the schedule is active, and the last run. openimport:queue:run ¶ Runs the queued runs now, oldest first (runs started in the admin wait in the queue). OpenImport's cron does the same every minute; the command is for stores without cron, deployments and tests. openimport:secrets:reencrypt ¶ After bin/magento encryption:key:change : encrypts every stored source password, private key and token again with the current key. Run it while the old key is still in app/etc/env.php . openimport:profiles:export [profile …] ¶ Writes profiles as JSON to standard output (all profiles, or the ones named by id or name): every setting, mapping and value map, never passwords, keys, tokens or upload tokens. Everything is checked first and listed as "create …" / "update …"; one problem and nothing is saved. --dry-run checks and lists without saving. Enter passwords and keys in the admin afterwards. openimport:doctor ¶ Checks what makes imports slow or stuck and says what to do: cron (has openimport_tick run in the last 10 minutes?), indexers on "Update on Save", PHP extensions and memory_limit , var/openimport writable, runs waiting longer than 15 minutes, runs "running" for more than 90 minutes. docs.text: Core bridge: how OpenImport writes data ¶ OpenImport never writes catalog, customer or stock tables itself. It prepares rows (read the file, map columns, transform values, filter rows) and hands them to Magento's own import engine, the one behind System › Data Transfer › Import. Whatever core would write for an equivalent CSV file is what OpenImport writes. The pieces ¶ Class Job Model\Source\MappedSource Core's AbstractSource over OpenImport's prepared rows. No temporary CSV file: core pulls rows from a generator. Missing columns become empty cells, like an empty CSV cell ("leave unchanged"). Model\Bridge\CoreImport Core's Import model plus getBunchIds() : the importexport_importdata rows this import validated (2.4.9 has getValidatedIds() , 2.4.7 and 2.4.8 do not). Model\Bridge\CoreImporter Validate, then (live runs only) add a core import history row, import, invalidate the entity's indexers, and always remove this run's bunches. Model\Bridge\ImportRequest / ImportResult / RowError What to run, and what came back (counts, errors with 0-based row positions, history id, time). Why the bunches are removed ¶ Core validation stores the validated rows in importexport_importdata and later imports the bunches whose ids the entity adapter collected. A dry run validates and stops, so its bunches would stay in the table. They are deleted by id at the end of every run, dry or live, and also when core throws. Import history ¶ Core's import updates the most recent history row of the current admin user (2.4.7, 2.4.8) or the row named in _import_history_id (2.4.9). A live OpenImport run adds its own history row right before the import and passes its id, so core's updates land on OpenImport's row on every version, never on someone else's import. The run appears under System › Data Transfer › Import History with its summary. The history row has no downloadable file yet (M1 writes the mapped rows there). Evidence ¶ Test/Integration/Bridge/CoreBridgeTest.php imports the same rows twice, once through core's CSV source (the admin path) and once through MappedSource , and compares the results field by field: simple products: new products with stock, special price, HTML description, disabled status, "Not Visible Individually", a store-view row; updates including __EMPTY__VALUE__ ; Replace and Delete; customers; dry run: nothing written, no bunch left behind; invalid rows with "skip errors": reported with their 0-based position, same outcome as core's CSV import; nothing imported with "stop on error"; import history row written and completed. Magento PHP Result (CI run 38402758703 ) 2.4.7-p10 8.2, 8.3 11 / 11 green 2.4.8-p5 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 11 / 11 green 2.4.9 8.3, 8.4 11 / 11 green Decision: MappedSource straight into core on every supported version. The temporary-CSV fallback planned in 02 · Architecture is not needed and is not built. What the spike found ¶ Core's error aggregator is shared. ProcessingErrorAggregator is a DI singleton. Core runs one import per admin request; OpenImport runs many per process (cron, CLI). Without clear() before each run, errors of earlier runs counted against the next run and stopped valid imports. CoreImporter clears it first. Store-view rows of new products need attribute_set_code and product_type . Core validates every row of a product that is new in the file as a new product. A store-view row with only sku , store_view_code and name is refused ("Product Type is invalid or not supported"), through the CSV source as well. OpenImport's store-view expansion (M1) copies both onto the rows it generates. An empty cell in a required attribute's column is an error, also for existing products. A file with a name or price column must fill it on every row. The mapping preview (M1) flags such rows before core sees them. Validated bunches stay in importexport_importdata unless removed. Removed by id after every run. Core's history update targets "the last row of this admin user" (2.4.7, 2.4.8) or _import_history_id (2.4.9). Adding OpenImport's own row right before the import and passing its id works on all three. Core reports 0-based positions of the rows it received. Mapping back to source line numbers is M1 (rows can be filtered out or expanded into store-view rows on the way). "Skip rows with errors" skips everything after one critical error. Core's row errors are critical by default, and the product, customer and other entities stop saving every row once the aggregator holds a critical error ( hasToBeTerminated() ), even with the skip-errors strategy, while the import still reports success (found in M1). With Skip rows with errors , OpenImport leaves the rows core rejected out ( SkipRowsSource ), validates the rest again and imports that; errors of every pass still point at the original rows. At most four validation passes; a critical error without a row stops the run with nothing imported.

docs.text: Exports ¶ An export profile (direction Export ) writes a file from a Magento export entity: products, customers, customer addresses, advanced pricing, stock sources (MSI) — every entity Magento's own System › Data Transfer › Export offers — plus OpenImport's Orders export. The rows come from Magento's own export code, so the columns are exactly those of a core export; OpenImport adds row filters, column mapping, formats and destinations, and runs it on a schedule. Steps ¶ What : direction Export and the entity. Where : the destination (download from the run page, server folder, SFTP, FTP, e-mail) and the file name. Placeholders in the file name: {entity} , {profile} , {date} (2026-10-14), {time} (143000), {datetime} , {run} , {ext} . Default {entity}-{datetime}.{ext} . File : CSV (delimiter, encoding UTF-8 or Windows-1252, BOM, line ending), Excel (.xlsx, sheet name), JSON (root key, pretty) or XML (root and record element names). Map : without a mapping every column is written as Magento exports it. With a mapping, each row is one column of the file: its name, the Magento column it comes from (or a fixed value), transforms and value maps — for example Preis = price with number(2, ",") for a German decimal comma. Rules : row filters on the Magento columns ( price > 15 , status in pending,processing , …). core_filters (attribute => value) are passed to Magento's export filter as well, for example sku = SUP- for a "like" filter. When : schedule, e-mails, and for orders "only new since the last run". A dry run writes the file into the run folder (download it from the run page to check it) but delivers it nowhere. A live run delivers it and keeps a copy in the run folder for "Keep run files for" days. Safety ¶ Cells that would run as a formula in a spreadsheet ( = , + , - , @ , tab, CR first) are prefixed with ' in CSV and Excel files (Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Safety › Protect exports against spreadsheet formulas ). Negative numbers are left alone. Excel files are written without any library: plain numbers become numeric cells, everything else stays text (SKUs with leading zeros survive). Excel's limit of 1,048,575 rows is enforced with a plain message. Destinations use the same encrypted secrets and the same SSRF, path and folder rules as sources (see Sources ). Orders ¶ The Orders entity is OpenImport's own (Magento has no order export). One row per order line by default (order, customer, totals, billing and shipping address, payment, shipments and tracking numbers repeated on every line; child lines of configurable and bundle products left out unless chosen), or one row per order. Filters: statuses, created from/until (UTC), store views, and Which orders : all, only orders this profile has not exported before, or new and changed orders (an order whose updated_at moved after its export, for status changes). Exported orders are remembered per profile ( openimport_export_mark ) after a successful live run; dry runs remember nothing. Typical use: a nightly "new orders" file for an ERP over SFTP. docs.text: File formats ¶ OpenImport reads CSV, Excel (.xlsx), JSON and XML files without any extra library. The format comes from the profile, or is detected from the file name and, when the name says nothing, from the first bytes of the file. Every reader returns rows of text keyed by column name, and every row keeps its position in the file, so an error says "row 18" and row 18 is what the merchant sees in Excel or a text editor. CSV and TSV ¶ Option Default Notes Delimiter auto Detected from the header line: comma, semicolon, tab or pipe (counted outside quotes). Enclosure " Doubled enclosures inside a cell ( "" ) are one quote. Encoding auto UTF-8 (with or without byte order mark), UTF-16 with byte order mark (Excel "Unicode text"), otherwise Windows-1252. Can be set to UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 or ISO-8859-15. First row is the header yes Without a header, columns are named column_1 , column_2 , … Quoted cells may hold delimiters and line breaks. Empty lines are skipped; row numbers still count them. Empty header cells become column_<n> ; duplicate headers become name (2) , name (3) . Short rows are filled with empty cells; extra cells without a header are dropped. The file is streamed: memory does not grow with the file size. Excel (.xlsx) ¶ Option Default Notes Sheet first sheet A sheet name (case does not matter) or its position (1, 2, …). First row is the header yes Text, numbers, booleans ( 1 / 0 ) and the cached results of formulas are read. Error cells ( #N/A ) are empty. Numbers come out as Excel shows them, without binary noise ( 0.3 , not 0.30000000000000004 ). Cells with a date or time format become 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31 14:30:00 (1900 and 1904 date systems). Row numbers are the sheet's own row numbers; empty rows are skipped. Old Excel files (.xls) are not supported: save them as .xlsx or .csv. Workbooks that would unpack to more than 512 MB are refused. The sheet is streamed with PHP's XMLReader; only the shared strings table is held in memory. JSON ¶ Option Default Notes Record path auto A dot path to the list of records, e.g. data.items . Auto: the document itself when it is a list, otherwise its only list of objects. Nested objects become dotted columns: {"stock": {"qty": 3}} gives the column stock.qty . Lists of plain values are joined with a comma ( ["red", "blue"] gives red,blue ); lists of objects are kept as JSON text in one column, for a transform to pick apart. true / false become 1 / 0 , null becomes an empty cell. Very large integers keep every digit. JSON files are read into memory, up to 50 MB by default. Use CSV or XML for larger files. XML ¶ Option Default Notes Record path children of the root /catalog/products/product (from the root) or //product (at any depth). Child elements become columns ( sku , stock.qty ), attributes become @id or price.@currency . Repeated plain children are joined with a comma ( <category>Men</category><category>Sale</category> gives Men,Sale ); repeated children with their own children are kept as JSON text. CDATA is read as text. The file is streamed record by record: memory does not grow with the file size. Files with a DOCTYPE are refused, and the parser never loads anything from the network (no XML entity attacks). Column names in JSON and XML files ¶ JSON and XML records do not all need the same fields. The column list shown in the mapping editor comes from the first 1,000 records; fields that only appear later are still imported when they are mapped by name.

docs.text: Mapping, store views and row filters ¶ Mapping ¶ A profile maps Magento fields (core import columns) to the file: Source column : the value comes from that column of the file. Fixed value : the same value for every row (for example attribute_set_code = Default , _website = base ). Transforms : an ordered list applied to the value (see Transforms and expressions ). A field with no source column and an expr transform computes its value from the whole row. Required : an empty result makes the row an error instead of sending it. Magento fields that are not mapped are not sent, so Magento leaves them unchanged. Columns of the file that are not mapped are ignored. The identifier field of the entity must be mapped: Entity Identifier Products ( catalog_product ), Stock & prices sku Advanced pricing sku , tier_price_website , tier_price_customer_group , tier_price_qty Customers, customers with address email , _website Customer addresses _email , _website , _entity_id Stock sources (MSI) sku , source_code Stock & prices ¶ The Stock & prices entity ( openimport_stock_price ) is made for supplier feeds: it can set qty , is_in_stock , price , special_price , special_price_from_date , special_price_to_date and cost of products that already exist, through Magento's own product import (with MSI, qty goes to the default source). SKUs the shop does not have are skipped and counted as skipped by behaviour ; they are never created. For quantities per MSI source, use the Stock sources entity. Auto-match ¶ The mapping editor suggests a mapping from the file's column names, in this order: the exact name; the name ignoring case, spaces, underscores, hyphens and dots ( Special Price → special_price ); known synonyms ( Artikelnummer → sku , Bestand / Menge → qty , Preis → price , Bezeichnung → name , E-Mail → email , Vorname → firstname …); and store-view columns ( name_de , name (de) , name [de] , store:de:name ). Each column is used once. When the first rows of a number field (price, cost, weight, qty …) are written with decimal commas ( 89,90 , 1.299,00 ), Auto-match adds the transform Decimal comma → dot to that field. Add required fields adds the fields Magento needs for new records with a proposed fixed value where there is a sensible one: the shop's default attribute set and website, product type simple , the default customer group, the default inventory source. Pick a column of the file instead, or change the value. Store-view values (products) ¶ Map a field as store:<store view code>:<field> , for example store:de:name . One row of the file then becomes the default row plus one row per store view that has at least one non-empty value. Store-view rows carry the SKU, the attribute set and the product type (Magento needs those for new products) and the store-view fields only. Row filters ¶ Row filters decide which rows of the file are imported, before mapping: Mode : include imports only the matching rows; exclude skips them. Match : all conditions or any condition. Conditions : a column, an operator and a value, or an expression . Operator Matches when the cell (trimmed, ignoring case) … equals , not_equals is / is not the value contains , not_contains , starts_with , ends_with contains / starts / ends with the value in , not_in is / is not one of a comma-separated list empty , not_empty is empty / not empty (a missing column is empty) greater_than , less_than is a number above / below the value (decimal commas allowed) regex matches the pattern Rows skipped by a filter are counted as "skipped by filter" on the run page, not as errors.

docs.text: Runs, dry runs and safety ¶ A run reads one file through a profile. Runs are queued (admin buttons, schedules, the CLI) and executed by OpenImport's own cron group or by bin/magento openimport:run ; never inside a web request. What happens in a run ¶ Read the file (see File formats ). Row filters skip rows (counted as filtered ). Mapping and transforms build Magento's import rows; a row that cannot be mapped becomes an error with its row number in your file. Behaviour : Only add new skips records that exist, Only update existing skips records that do not (counted as skipped ). Delta (when switched on): a record whose prepared rows are exactly what the last successful run of this profile sent is skipped (counted as unchanged ). Changing the profile's source, format, filters, behaviour, mapping or value maps forgets the stored state, and a run with full ignores it. Each line of the file is compared on its own, so a file with one line per store view (or several addresses or tier prices per record) only sends the lines that changed. Magento validates and imports the rows with its own import engine. Its errors are reported against the rows of your file, not against Magento's internal row numbers. Prepared rows are written to the run folder ( var/openimport/runs/<run id>/ ), so memory use does not grow with the file. Dry runs ¶ A dry run does everything except the import: Magento validates every row, and OpenImport compares the prepared rows with what the shop has now. The run page shows the totals (new, changed, unchanged, deleted) and a sample of up to 200 records per kind with before → after for every changed field. Comparison follows Magento's rules: empty cells change nothing, numbers compare as numbers (12.50 = 12.5), Yes/No equal 1/0. docs.text: Schedules and cron ¶ Magento Open Source has no scheduled import or export (that is Adobe Commerce only). OpenImport brings its own, run by Magento's normal cron. What you need ¶ Magento's cron must run every minute, as for any store: * * * * * php /var/www/html/bin/magento cron:run OpenImport adds its own cron group, openimport , which runs in a separate process. A long import never holds up Magento's default jobs (indexers, e-mails), and they never hold up an import. Job When What it does openimport_tick every minute Queues the runs of profiles whose schedule is due, then runs queued runs until the minute's time budget is used. openimport_cleanup hourly (minute 17) Removes old run folders, unused uploads and old schedule records; marks runs that stopped without finishing as failed. Without cron, queued runs wait. bin/magento openimport:queue:run does the same work as the tick by hand (see Command line ). Profile schedules ¶ A profile's schedule is a preset (every hour, every day at 02:00, weekdays at 06:00, …) or a 5-field cron expression: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Lists ( 1,15 ), ranges ( 8-18 ), steps ( */15 ) and names ( mon-fri , jan ) work. Times are read in the store's time zone (Stores › Configuration › General › Locale Options › Timezone), so 0 2 * * * means 02:00 local time, also across daylight-saving changes. A schedule only fires while the profile's Schedule is on switch is on. New and duplicated profiles start with it off: run a dry run first, then switch it on. Scheduled runs are live runs. The safety threshold still applies: a scheduled Delete or Replace run that would remove more than the threshold stops with "needs confirmation" and waits for someone to confirm it on the run page. Exactly once ¶ Each due minute fires once, even when: two cron processes overlap (a slow cron:run and the next one): the first process records schedule:<profile>:<minute> in openimport_lock ; the second finds the record and does nothing; cron comes late: a due minute missed by up to 10 minutes still fires, once. Missed by more, it is skipped, and the next due minute fires as usual (no flood of catch-up runs after downtime); a run of the same profile is still going: the new run waits in the queue until the profile lock is free. Two runs of one profile never run at the same time, and two live imports of the same entity never run at the same time (products and Stock & prices share the product entity). Housekeeping ¶ Run files (the uploaded or fetched source, prepared rows, output) are removed after "Keep run files for" days (Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport). The run, its counts and stored errors stay. Uploaded files no profile uses any more are removed after two days. A run that has been "running" for more than 90 minutes without a live lock (the PHP process died, the server restarted) is marked failed with "The run stopped without finishing", so the profile can run again. E-mails ¶ Each profile says when to send an e-mail (step 6): never, on failure (failed, finished with errors, needs confirmation) or always, to the comma-separated addresses, or, when empty, to the admin who created the profile. The e-mail carries the result, the counts, the run message, a note on errors and a link to the run page. It uses the store's e-mail settings (Stores › Configuration › General › Store Email Addresses, "General Contact" as sender) and the template OpenImport: a run finished , which can be customised under Marketing › Email Templates.

docs.text: Security ¶ OpenImport fetches files from other servers, reads formats that can carry attacks, and writes into the catalog. This page lists what the module does about that, what the settings control, and what remains your job. Admin actions ¶ Every controller is behind an ACL resource: View profiles , Create and edit profiles , Run profiles , Confirm runs above the safety limit , View runs and error reports , plus the configuration section. Roles that may view but not edit get a read-only form. Everything that changes state is a POST with Magento's form key; everything that reads is a GET. File answers go through Magento's FileFactory , never a raw path. Uploads: 256 MB at most, only .csv .tsv .txt .xlsx .json .xml , stored under a random token in var/openimport/tmp and removed by housekeeping. A token is accepted only if it names a file in that folder (no .. , no other folder). Sample and preview answers, error reports and the run page escape every value; messages from Magento's importer are shown as text. Remote sources and destinations ¶ Web address: http and https only, no credentials in the URL. The host is resolved and every address must be public: loopback, private (RFC 1918), link-local (169.254.x, the cloud metadata address), carrier-grade NAT, IPv6 ULA and link-local, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 are refused. The request is pinned to the checked address ( CURLOPT_RESOLVE ), every redirect hop is checked again, basic auth and bearer tokens are sent to the first host only, and downloads stop at 256 MB. Hosts you trust (a warehouse system on the LAN) go into Allowed private hosts . Server folder: only var/openimport and the folders listed in Allowed folders (absolute paths, real paths compared, so symlinks out of the sandbox do not help). Patterns pick files; the module never runs them. SFTP / FTP: host names are resolved and checked like URLs. SFTP uses phpseclib (password or private key, with an optional passphrase); FTP uses PHP's ftp_* functions with TLS when switched on, passive mode. Nothing is executed on the remote side; the module lists, downloads, uploads, renames and deletes inside the configured folder. E-mail destination: attachments are capped (setting), the recipients come from the profile, never from the file. Credentials ¶ Passwords, private keys, passphrases and tokens are encrypted with Magento's encryptor and stored under a separate secrets key of the profile. They are never written to logs, run messages, JSON profile exports, the admin form (the form shows "stored" and lets you replace a secret, not read it) or the error report. After a key rotation run bin/magento openimport:secrets:reencrypt . File formats ¶ XML: streamed with XMLReader ; documents with a DOCTYPE are refused, so there is no entity expansion and no external entity. The parser never resolves URLs. XLSX: read from the zip with size checks; a workbook whose parts would unpack to more than 512 MB is refused (zip bombs). Only the parts the reader needs are opened. CSV written by the module (error reports, exports): cells starting with = + - @ or a tab are prefixed with an apostrophe when the formula guard setting is on (default), so a product name cannot become a spreadsheet formula. Expressions and transforms: the expression language is parsed once per run into a small AST and evaluated without eval ; it has no access to PHP functions, files or the database. Division by zero and type errors become row errors. Writing into Magento ¶ Magento's own importer validates and writes every row. OpenImport does not write catalog tables itself. Runs that would delete or replace more records than the profile's safety threshold stop and wait for a typed confirmation by a user with the Confirm runs above the safety limit resource. New profiles always start with a dry run. One run per profile and one live import per core entity at a time (database locks with heartbeats), so two cron ticks cannot import the same file twice. What stays with you ¶ Protect var/openimport like the rest of var/ : it holds uploaded and fetched files and the error reports. Give SFTP/FTP accounts the smallest folder they need; the module cannot escape its folder, but the account could. Keep Magento's cron under a user that cannot write to the code base. Report problems privately, see SECURITY.md .

Transforms and expressions ¶ Every mapped field can run a list of transforms, in order, on the value taken from the source column (or the static value). Each step gets the previous step's result. Empty values stay empty in number and date transforms, so an empty price never turns into 0. A value a transform cannot handle (text in a number transform, an impossible date) becomes a row error naming the field, the step and the value; the rest of the file still imports. Text ¶ Transform Arguments Example trim – " Shirt " → Shirt lower , upper , title – red shirt → Red Shirt (title) replace find, replace (default: nothing) replace("cm", " cm") : 10cm → 10 cm regex pattern, replace (default: nothing) regex("^ART-(\d+)$", "$1") : ART-0042 → 0042 strip_html –

Soft & warm

→ Soft & warm prefix , suffix text prefix("DE-") : 42 → DE-42 (empty values stay empty) default value used when the value is empty split separator, position (1 = first, -1 = last) split(";", 2) : a;b;c → b join separator, column, … join(" ", "Brand") : Shirt → Shirt ACME ; empty parts are left out Regex patterns are written without delimiters and are Unicode-aware; (?i) at the start ignores case. A pattern that backtracks too much fails the row instead of hanging the run. Numbers ¶ Numbers are read the way files write them: 1234.5 , 1,5 , 1.234,56 , 1,234.56 , 1 234,5 , 1'234.50 . Transform Arguments Example decimal_comma – for files with decimal commas: 1.234,50 → 1234.5 , 1.234 → 1234 number decimals (optional), decimal separator . or , (optional) number(2) : 5 → 5.00 ; number(2, ",") : 12.5 → 12,50 (exports) math operator ( + - * / , × ÷ , or add , subtract , multiply , divide ), operand math("*", 1.19) round decimals (default 2), mode half_up / up / down / ending , ending round(2, "ending", .99) : 12.30 → 12.99 price_adjust percent, decimals (default 2) price_adjust(10) : 19.99 → 21.99 round with mode ending moves to the next price with the given cents: 12.30 → 12.99 , 12.99 stays, and with .49 : 12.60 → 13.49 . Dates ¶ date(from_format, to_format) with PHP date letters ( d.m.Y , m/d/Y , Y-m-d H:i:s ). from_format auto (the default) accepts ISO dates ( 2024-01-31 , with or without time) and German dates ( 31.01.2024 , with or without time). to_format defaults to Y-m-d . Impossible dates such as 31.02.2024 are row errors. No time-zone conversion. Value maps ¶ map replaces whole values using the field's value map ( Ja → 1 , rot → Red ). Case and surrounding spaces are ignored by default; values not in the map pass through unchanged, or are row errors when the map is strict. Expressions ¶ expr(expression) computes a value from the whole source row. Expressions are parsed once per run; there is no eval and no access to PHP functions. Element Syntax Column {Column Name} (a } inside a name is written }} ) Current value value Text 'text' or "text" (a doubled quote inside is one quote) Number 42 , 1.5 , 1e3 (start with a digit: 0.5 , not .5 ) Arithmetic + - * / % Join text . ( {Brand} . ' ' . {Name} ) Compare = != <> < <= > >= (numbers as numbers, text ignoring case) Logic and , or , not , true , false Functions: IF(condition, then, else) , ROUND(number, decimals) , CONCAT(…) , LOWER(text) , UPPER(text) , TRIM(text) , COALESCE(…) (first non-empty), LEN(text) , NUMBER(text) , REPLACE(text, find, replace) , CONTAINS(text, part) , MIN(…) , MAX(…) , ABS(number) . Function names and keywords ignore case. Rules: Arithmetic with an empty value gives an empty value: {Special price} * 1.19 stays empty when there is no special price. Text that is not a number in arithmetic, and division by zero, are row errors. Empty text, 0 and false are false in conditions; everything else is true. Whole numbers keep every digit; decimals have 15 significant digits. Expressions are limited to 2,000 characters and 40 levels of nesting. Examples: IF({Stock} > 0, 1, 0) ROUND(NUMBER({Preis}) * 1.19, 2) CONCAT({Brand}, ' ', {Model}, ' ', {Color}) IF(CONTAINS({Category}, 'sale'), {Price} * 0.9, {Price}) COALESCE({EAN}, {GTIN}, {Supplier SKU}) Your own transforms ¶ Implement Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Transform\TransformProviderInterface and add the class to the providers argument of Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Transform\TransformPool in your module's di.xml . A provider may also replace a built-in transform by using its name.

docs.text: Every mapped field can run a list of transforms, in order, on the value taken from the source column (or the static value). Each step gets the previous step's result. Empty values stay empty in number and date transforms, so an empty price never turns into 0. A value a transform cannot handle (text in a number transform, an impossible date) becomes a row error naming the field, the step and the value; the rest of the file still imports.
